title: Re-clip a cabinet door that has dropped off its lower clip-on hinge, holding it square, then shut it
instruction: This cabinet door has come off its bottom hinge. Hang it back on both hinges and close it.
context: General maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071, about 1.5 million in the US) fix cabinet doors in flats, hotels, schools and hospitals, and carpenters (47-2031, about 0.9 million) hang and adjust them. Most modern kitchen and bathroom cabinets hang their doors on tool-free clip-on cup hinges. A door that is pulled or leaned on pops off one mounting plate and hangs from the other, sagging under its own weight. That is a routine work order. The hinge arm only hooks onto its plate with the door held square; pressed while the door droops, it misses the plate's nose and will not click. So one hand lifts the door's free corner and holds it square while the other presses the arm home. Closed on its upper hinge alone, the door hangs crooked and the loose arm flaps inside.
setup: Centimetres; x forward from the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench. A painted plasterboard wall section (1.25 thick, 74 wide, 62 tall) stands fixed on the bench at x 70 to 71.25, y -32 to 42. On it hangs a wall cabinet, fixed, its opening towards the robot: 30 wide (y -10 to 20), 40 tall (underside 3 above the bench), 30 deep (x 40 to 70), in 1.8 white melamine-faced particleboard with a 0.8 back. Its door is 29.6 x 39.6 x 1.6 grey melamine-faced particleboard, 1.3 kg with its black zinc knob (head 3.2 across, 1.4 thick, standing 3.5 proud of the door, 3.5 from the free edge and 6 up from the door's bottom). It hangs on two 110-degree clip-on 35 mm cup hinges (nickel-plated steel arms 6.5 x 1.8 x 1.5, about 0.1 kg each) on the cabinet's right-hand side. Cups are 9 from the door's ends, with centres 12.2 and 33.8 above the bench. Zinc cruciform mounting plates are on the right side's inside face, centred 3.7 behind its front edge. The door turns about a vertical line at the cabinet's front right corner (x 40, y -10.1); shut, it stands 3 mm off the carcass front. The hinges' springs pull it shut over the last 35 degrees. Start: the door stands open 90 degrees, its free edge at x 10.2, hanging from the upper hinge alone. It has sagged 4 degrees about that hinge in its own plane, so its free bottom corner is 2.1 low (1.2 above the bench). The lower hinge's arm is off its plate, 1.5 behind it and 1.2 proud of it. Distractors, loose on the bench and not part of the task: a ceramic mug (11.4 x 9 x 8 tall, 0.30 kg) at x 55, y 31; a kitchen sponge (7 x 10 x 3.3, 0.02 kg) at x 62, y -22; a No. 2 Phillips screwdriver (18.8 long, 0.10 kg) lying along x, from x 38 to 57 at y -25.
scoring: From the door's angles and the lower arm's position (real trial: the click, a feeler and an angle gauge). Clipped: the lower arm has clicked onto its plate. It clicks when pressed to within 1 mm of home with the door within 0.5 degrees of square, its free corner within 2.6 mm of its square height. A clicked arm stays on and keeps the door square. Shut: the door within 1 degree of its stop, its free edge within 5 mm of shut. Clear: every finger point of both grippers 3 cm or more from the door (with its knob and cups) and from the lower arm. Still: the door's free edge moving under 1 cm/s. 1.0: clipped, shut, clear and still, all held for 3 s. 0.5: clipped, clear and still otherwise (door left open, or shut for under 3 s). 0.25: clipped, but a gripper within 3 cm or the door moving at the end. 0: not clipped, whatever else, including a door shut on its upper hinge alone.
reset_notes: Press the lower arm's release lever and take the arm off its plate. Open the door to 90 degrees and let it hang from the upper hinge, sagged onto its free corner, the arm hanging off its plate. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; real sizes and masses. Cabinet and door are boxes. Hinges are simplified: the door hangs on a sag joint about the upper hinge (-4 to +3 deg) carrying its swing joint; the loose lower arm slides 12 mm towards its plate on a light spring. The click is a rule: pressed to 1 mm from home with the door within 0.5 deg of square, both joints lock. No hook-on-plate contact is modelled. Closing springs: 0.6 N m/rad over the last 35 deg. Mug, sponge and screwdriver are SimReady props.
